review_budget._comment: One logical doc-review plan holds one or more physical batches. Whichever limit is hit first opens the next batch; both boundaries are inclusive, so 12 files and exactly 200000 bytes stay in one batch and the 13th file or the 200001st byte starts another. Consumed by scripts/resolve-review-profile.js; contract in docs/features/doc-review-phasing/2-tech-spec.md section 4 Step 4.
review_budget._sizing: The corpus median feature doc is 397 lines, so 12 median files are roughly 190 KB — the two limits bite at about the same place, which is why neither alone is the budget. A single file larger than max_bytes forms its own batch and is REPORTED as over-budget rather than skipped: there is nothing left to split, and dropping it would be the silent truncation the loud-split rule exists to prevent.

doc_roles._comment: Artifact roles: does this document owe alignment with the current code? Consumed by scripts/lib/doc-metadata.js; contract in docs/features/doc-review-phasing/2-tech-spec.md section 3.1. This is the per-repo customization surface — a project whose docs are laid out differently edits path_defaults here rather than the code.
doc_roles._matching: path_defaults are ordered and first-match-wins, over a path split on '/' with empty segments dropped. scope=segment tests the pattern against EVERY segment including the basename, which is what lets one rule cover both 'review-log-x.md' and 'review-log-x/rounds-1-9.md'. scope=first_segment tests the first segment only, because 'skills' means something as a repo root directory and nothing as a folder inside a feature. A path matching no rule resolves to `fallback`.
doc_roles._contract: closed_set and fallback are RECORDED here, not configured: doc-metadata.js pins both (CONTRACT_ROLES) and ignores any other value. Editing them changes nothing, by design — a config that could set fallback to a non-authority role, or add a fifth role, would exempt documents wholesale, since owing code alignment is defined as BEING `Current authority`. path_defaults and metadata are the per-repo surface.
